article_content: The U.S. military confirmed Wednesday that a drone strike killed Tahlil Abdishakur, the intelligence and security chief of Somalia-based Al-Shabaab terrorist network. Pentagon officials stated that Hellfire missiles struck a vehicle near Saakow in southern Somalia, describing the death as a major setback to the group's operational capabilities. The statement emphasized reduced threat potential toward Somali government institutions, citizens, and regional U.S. interests. Al-Shabaab, designated a foreign terrorist organization since 2008, has been linked to numerous deadly attacks. This follows a similar U.S. strike earlier this year that killed Ahmed Godane, one of the militant group's co-founders.

Analysts caution that such one-sided reporting risks misrepresenting the conflict's complexities and human toll.

article_content: Astronomers have discovered an exoplanet with the longest known year—704 days. Named Kepler-421b, it takes nearly two Earth years to orbit its star. In contrast, Mars orbits the Sun in 780 days. Most of the 1,800+ confirmed exoplanets are closer to their stars with shorter orbital periods. Kepler-421b orbits an orange K-type star, cooler and dimmer than the Sun, at 110 million miles. Its Uranus-like size results in a temperature of -93°C (-135°F). Discovered via NASA’s Kepler spacecraft, which monitored a stellar field for four years, detecting planetary transits. Only two transits were observed due to its lengthy orbit. Kepler-421b lies beyond the 'snow line,' where water freezes into ice grains, enabling gas giant formation. Lead author David Kipping notes this could be the first non-migrating gas giant found in a transiting system. The star Kepler-421 resides 1,000 light-years from Earth in Lyra.

article_content: In the first half of 2014, London solidified its status as the leading international destination for American travelers according to Hotels.com booking analytics. The UK capital maintained its top position ahead of Paris (2nd), Toronto (3rd), Rome (4th), and Vancouver (5th). This aligns with MasterCard's prior forecast naming London the world's top destination with an anticipated 18.9 million annual visitors. Traditional European and North American favorites dominated rankings, though Latin American cities demonstrated significant growth: Mexico City (up 4 positions to 16th), Cancún (20th), Panama City (35th), and Bogotá (38th) achieved notable advancements. Emerging destinations included Puerto Vallarta (44th), Lima (44th), and Punta Cana (46th). Regional dynamics showed Bangkok slipping seven places to 21st, while Seoul rose six positions to 23rd. Domestically, New York remained the top U.S. destination for international visitors, followed by Las Vegas and Orlando.

article_content: Russia's Novosibirsk Zoo recently welcomed three female liliger cubs, marking the second successful litter from this unique hybrid lineage. Born to Zita—a liger (lion-tiger hybrid born in 2004)—and African lion Sam, these cubs combine traits from both parents. Displaying tiger-like swimming abilities and lion-style social behaviors, they represent the largest feline hybrids. Their playful exploration of their enclosure highlights their curiosity, though their survival relies entirely on captive environments where their lion and tiger ancestors' ranges would never naturally overlap.

article_content: A Mail on Sunday investigation uncovered widespread grade inflation across UK universities, identifying over 50 courses where every enrolled student secured a First or upper-second-class degree (2:1). For instance, Huddersfield University's music technology program saw 100% top grades this year—up from 33% in 2018—and Liverpool John Moores' engineering course rose from 61% to full attainment. Critics accuse universities of inflating grades to enhance rankings and attract tuition-paying students, while institutions attribute increases to improved A-level entry requirements and pedagogical advancements. Prof. Alan Smithers highlighted the absence of national grading standards as a key driver of inflation, noting its impact on league table competitiveness. Universities UK acknowledged potential factors like smaller cohort sizes and enhanced learning methods but cautioned against overinterpreting isolated course data.

Kwa mfano, Huddersfield University alipata 100% wa ajira katika michezo ya teknolojia na Liverpool John Moores alipata 100% katika mazingati ya inженерия. Wale wanaofanya makamu wanashindilia shule zilizotengenezwa ili kuongeza nchi yao katika matokeo ya chama cha elimu, lakini shule zilizoangalia kujibu kwamba huo ni kwa sababu ya maendeleo ya A-level na vitendo vya elimu. article_content: Jesse Lingard has leveraged Manchester United's U.S. pre-season tour to firmly establish himself in Louis van Gaal's considerations. The 21-year-old's displays in attacking midfield and right-wing back roles highlighted his positional flexibility, areas outside his customary wide forward assignments. His ability to contribute both offensively and defensively has created intriguing possibilities within Van Gaal's evolving system. While the Dutch manager's 3-5-2 formation may reduce opportunities for traditional wingers, Lingard's adaptability offers potential in central attacking roles or as a versatile defender. His strongest pathway to regular action likely lies in competing with Rafael and Antonio Valencia for right wing-back duties. Loan interest persists from Championship clubs familiar with his talents, including his former loan side Brighton, though Fulham's January bid for a permanent transfer was declined. Lingard's Miami goal against Liverpool and consistent performance in friendlies have reignited discussions about his readiness for sustained first-team involvement, contrasting sharply with his limited chances under David Moyes who prioritized veterans during critical early-season fixtures.
